conditions: Linear two-conductor capacitor with equal and opposite conductor charges, fixed geometry and linear dielectric; V is nonzero and defined using the same conductor as Q.

symbols.V: Potential of reference conductor minus other conductor

spoken_aliases: c equals q divided by v
capacitance equals the charge on the reference conductor divided by the voltage across the capacitor

evidence: For a linear two-conductor capacitor with equal and opposite plate charges and fixed geometry and dielectric properties, charge is proportional to potential difference. The proportionality constant C is positive; for nonzero voltage, divide Q=CV by V. This is a constitutive definition, not a claim for nonlinear capacitors.
Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-2/pages/8-key-equations. Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
